nodes.label: graphify AGENTS.md block
nodes.rationale: A short `## graphify` section graphify installs into a project's AGENTS.md. It announces that the project has a graphify knowledge graph at graphify-out/ and carries a three-item Rules list telling any agent how to use it.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: The project's graphify knowledge graph lives in the `graphify-out/` directory. Everything the rules point an agent at — GRAPH_REPORT.md and wiki/index.md — is a file inside it.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Rule 1: before answering architecture or codebase questions, read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` for god nodes and community structure. It is the orientation artifact the agent consults first.

nodes.label: god nodes
nodes.rationale: One of the two things GRAPH_REPORT.md is read for — the highly connected hub entities of the graph that an agent should know before answering an architecture question.

nodes.label: community structure
nodes.rationale: The second thing GRAPH_REPORT.md is read for: the clustering of the graph into communities, which the report exposes alongside god nodes.

nodes.label: wiki/index.md navigation
nodes.rationale: Rule 2: if `graphify-out/wiki/index.md` exists, the agent should navigate it instead of reading raw files. The rule is conditional on the wiki having been generated.

nodes.label: reading raw source files
nodes.rationale: The default agent behaviour the rules displace: browsing the project's raw files directly. The wiki index is to be navigated 'instead of reading raw files'.

nodes.label: architecture / codebase questions
nodes.rationale: The class of question the rules govern. The contract fires 'before answering architecture or codebase questions' — those questions are what makes reading GRAPH_REPORT.md obligatory rather than optional.

nodes.label: graphify update .
nodes.rationale: Rule 3: after modifying code files in a session, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current. It is the write-back half of the contract, closing the loop after the agent edits code.

nodes.label: AST-only, no API cost
nodes.rationale: The stated property of `graphify update .`: it is AST-only and incurs no API cost. That is the reason the rule can demand it after every code-modifying session without a token budget concern.

nodes.label: graph-first agent workflow
nodes.rationale: The shape the three rules together impose on a session: orient from the graph report, navigate the wiki rather than raw files, and re-extract after edits. Read the graph first, write it back last.

nodes.label: graphify: skill over a Python library
nodes.rationale: graphify is a Claude Code skill backed by a Python library. The skill orchestrates the library, and the library can be used standalone — so the orchestration layer and the computation layer are deliberately separable.

nodes.label: Seven-stage pipeline
nodes.rationale: The core flow is detect() -> extract() -> build_graph() -> cluster() -> analyze() -> report() -> export(). Each stage is a single function living in its own module.

nodes.label: Stage isolation invariant
nodes.rationale: Pipeline stages communicate only through plain Python dicts and NetworkX graphs: no shared state, and no side effects outside `graphify-out/`. This is what makes each stage independently testable and re-runnable.

nodes.label: detect.py — collect_files(root)
nodes.rationale: `detect.py` owns the first pipeline stage: `collect_files(root)` turns a directory into a filtered list of `[Path]`. It also holds the `CODE_EXTENSIONS` registry that decides which suffixes are in scope.

nodes.label: extract.py — extract(path)
nodes.rationale: `extract.py` owns the second stage: `extract(path)` maps one file path to a `{nodes, edges}` dict. It also carries the per-language `extract_<lang>` functions and the suffix dispatch that selects among them.

nodes.label: build.py — build_graph(extractions)
nodes.rationale: `build.py` owns the third stage: `build_graph(extractions)` folds a list of extraction dicts into a single `nx.Graph`. It is the point at which per-file extractions become one graph.

nodes.label: cluster.py — cluster(G)
nodes.rationale: `cluster.py` owns the fourth stage: `cluster(G)` takes a graph and returns the same graph with a `community` attribute stamped on each node. Community structure is therefore an annotation on the graph, not a separate artifact.

nodes.label: analyze.py — analyze(G)
nodes.rationale: `analyze.py` owns the fifth stage: `analyze(G)` turns a graph into an analysis dict containing god nodes, surprises, and questions.

nodes.label: report.py — render_report(G, analysis)
nodes.rationale: `report.py` owns the sixth stage: `render_report(G, analysis)` consumes both the graph and the analysis dict and returns the GRAPH_REPORT.md string.

nodes.label: export.py — export(G, out_dir, ...)
nodes.rationale: `export.py` owns the final stage: `export(G, out_dir, ...)` writes the graph out as an Obsidian vault, `graph.json`, `graph.html`, and `graph.svg`.

nodes.label: callflow_html.py — write_callflow_html
nodes.rationale: `callflow_html.py` provides `write_callflow_html(...)`, which reads existing graphify-out files and renders Mermaid architecture / call-flow HTML. It is a downstream view, not a pipeline stage.

nodes.label: ingest.py — ingest(url, ...)
nodes.rationale: `ingest.py` provides `ingest(url, ...)`, which fetches a URL and saves it as a file in the corpus directory. It is how external material enters the pipeline before `detect()` sees it.

nodes.label: cache.py — semantic cache check/save
nodes.rationale: `cache.py` exposes `check_semantic_cache` / `save_semantic_cache`, which split a set of files into a (cached, uncached) pair so already-extracted files need not be extracted again.

nodes.label: security.py — validation helpers
nodes.rationale: `security.py` holds the validation helpers that turn a URL, path, or label into a validated value or raise. It is the single choke point every piece of external input must pass through.

nodes.label: validate.py — validate_extraction(data)
nodes.rationale: `validate.py` provides `validate_extraction(data)`, which raises on schema errors. It enforces the extraction schema before `build_graph()` is allowed to consume the extraction.

nodes.label: serve.py — start_server(graph_path)
nodes.rationale: `serve.py` provides `start_server(graph_path)`, which turns a graph file path into an MCP stdio server. Serving is a read path over an already-built graph, outside the build pipeline.

nodes.label: watch.py — watch(root, flag_path)
nodes.rationale: `watch.py` provides `watch(root, flag_path)`, which observes a directory and writes a flag file on change. It also owns the `_WATCHED_EXTENSIONS` registry.

nodes.label: benchmark.py — run_benchmark(graph_path)
nodes.rationale: `benchmark.py` provides `run_benchmark(graph_path)`, which takes a graph file and produces a corpus-vs-subgraph token comparison — the measurement behind the claim that a scoped subgraph is cheaper than the raw corpus.

nodes.label: Extraction output schema {nodes, edges}
nodes.rationale: Every extractor returns the same shape: `nodes` each with `id`, `label`, `source_file`, `source_location`; and `edges` each with `source`, `target`, `relation` (calls|imports|uses|...) and `confidence`. One schema for every language is what lets `build_graph()` be language-agnostic.

nodes.label: Three-tier confidence labelling
nodes.rationale: Every edge carries one of exactly three confidence labels — EXTRACTED, INFERRED, or AMBIGUOUS — so a consumer can tell a fact read out of the source from a deduction the tool made.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED confidence
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED means the relationship is explicitly stated in the source — for example an import statement or a direct call.

nodes.label: INFERRED confidence
nodes.rationale: INFERRED means the relationship is a reasonable deduction rather than a verbatim statement — for example an edge produced by the call-graph second pass, or co-occurrence in context.

nodes.label: AMBIGUOUS confidence
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS means the relationship is uncertain; such edges are flagged for human review in GRAPH_REPORT.md rather than silently kept or dropped.

nodes.label: Adding a new language extractor (5 steps)
nodes.rationale: A new language is added by five steps: write `extract_<lang>(path: Path) -> dict` in `extract.py`; register the suffix in `extract()` dispatch and `collect_files()`; add the suffix to `CODE_EXTENSIONS` and `_WATCHED_EXTENSIONS`; add the tree-sitter package to `pyproject.toml`; and add a fixture plus tests in `tests/test_languages.py`.

nodes.label: Tree-sitter extractor pattern
nodes.rationale: Every language extractor follows the same shape: tree-sitter parse, walk nodes, collect `nodes` and `edges`, then a call-graph second pass. Parsing is local and deterministic — a tree-sitter grammar, not a model.

nodes.label: Call-graph second pass
nodes.rationale: After the direct walk, each extractor runs a call-graph second pass that emits `calls` edges marked INFERRED — deductions kept explicitly separate from the verbatim EXTRACTED edges of the first pass.

nodes.label: Suffix registries: CODE_EXTENSIONS and _WATCHED_EXTENSIONS
nodes.rationale: Which file suffixes graphify handles is declared in two registries that must be kept in step: `CODE_EXTENSIONS` in `detect.py` (what gets collected) and `_WATCHED_EXTENSIONS` in `watch.py` (what triggers a change flag).

nodes.label: All external input passes through security.py
nodes.rationale: The stated invariant is that all external input passes through `graphify/security.py` before use — a single validation boundary rather than per-call-site checks, covering URLs, fetched content, graph file paths, and node labels.

nodes.label: validate_url() — http/https only
nodes.rationale: `validate_url()` restricts URLs to the http and https schemes, rejecting anything else before a fetch is attempted.

nodes.label: _NoFileRedirectHandler — blocks file:// redirects
nodes.rationale: Scheme validation at request time is not enough because a remote server can redirect; `_NoFileRedirectHandler` blocks `file://` redirects so an approved http URL cannot be bounced into the local filesystem.

nodes.label: safe_fetch() / safe_fetch_text() — size cap + timeout
nodes.rationale: Fetched content goes through `safe_fetch()` / `safe_fetch_text()`, which impose a size cap and a timeout so a hostile or broken endpoint cannot exhaust memory or hang the run.

nodes.label: validate_graph_path() — must resolve inside graphify-out/
nodes.rationale: `validate_graph_path()` requires a supplied graph file path to resolve inside `graphify-out/`, so a caller cannot point the tool at an arbitrary file on disk.

nodes.label: sanitize_label() — strip, cap, escape
nodes.rationale: Node labels pass through `sanitize_label()`, which strips control characters, caps the label at 256 characters, and HTML-escapes it — because labels end up rendered into HTML/SVG exports.

nodes.label: SECURITY.md threat model
nodes.rationale: ARCHITECTURE.md lists the concrete validation helpers but defers the full threat model to `SECURITY.md`; that document is the authority for what the validation boundary is defending against.

nodes.label: One test file per module
nodes.rationale: The test layout mirrors the module layout: one test file per module under `tests/`, run with `pytest tests/ -q`. Language extractors additionally get a fixture in `tests/fixtures/` and cases in `tests/test_languages.py`.

nodes.label: Pure unit tests — no network, no external side effects
nodes.rationale: All tests are pure unit tests: no network calls, and no file system side effects outside `tmp_path`. The suite is therefore hermetic and reproducible on any host.

nodes.label: Analysis dict — god nodes, surprises, questions
nodes.rationale: `analyze(G)` returns an analysis dict whose named contents are god nodes, surprises, and questions — the interpretive layer over the raw graph, kept as data so `report()` can render it.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: GRAPH_REPORT.md is the human-facing narrative rendered by `render_report(G, analysis)`; it is also where AMBIGUOUS edges are surfaced for human review.

nodes.label: NetworkX graph as the shared in-memory representation
nodes.rationale: From `build_graph()` onward the currency of the pipeline is an `nx.Graph`: cluster, analyze, report, and export all take the NetworkX graph as input, which is what keeps the stages composable without shared state.

nodes.label: Export artifacts — vault, graph.json, graph.html, graph.svg
nodes.rationale: `export()` emits four artifacts from one graph: an Obsidian vault, `graph.json`, `graph.html`, and `graph.svg` — several views of the same data rather than one canonical output format.

nodes.label: MCP stdio server
nodes.rationale: `start_server(graph_path)` exposes a built graph over an MCP stdio server, which is how an agent consumes the graph without re-running the pipeline.

nodes.label: Semantic cache (cached / uncached split)
nodes.rationale: The semantic cache is modelled as a split of a file set into (cached, uncached) via `check_semantic_cache`, with `save_semantic_cache` writing results back — so only the uncached remainder needs fresh extraction.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ — the only write surface
nodes.rationale: `graphify-out/` is the single directory the pipeline is permitted to write to, and the directory a graph path must resolve inside to be accepted. It is both the output surface and a containment boundary.

nodes.label: graphify benchmark harness
nodes.rationale: graphify's own open harness runs every competing system under identical conditions — same model, same token budgets, same grader. It has two suites: a memory suite (`memory/`) and a code suite (`crosstool/`). Because it is graphify's own harness, every figure in this document carries that as a condition.

nodes.label: Five-stage benchmark pipeline
nodes.rationale: Every run follows ingest (build) -> index (store) -> search (retrieve) -> answer (Kimi K2.6) -> grade (key-fact coverage). Competing systems are plugged in as adapters at the ingest/index/search stages while answer and grade stay shared.

nodes.label: Fairness rules
nodes.rationale: The declared conditions under which every number was measured: one model for every LLM role, one shared local embedder where the system allows it, identical token budgets with a spend ledger and `--max-spend`, and AST-only graph builds with no LLM. These rules are what make the cross-system comparison meaningful.

nodes.label: Kimi K2.6 as the one shared model
nodes.rationale: One model fills every LLM role in the memory benchmark — Kimi K2.6 via Moonshot — as reader, as answerer, and as judge. Adapters for mem0 and supermemory are wired through a proxy so even their internal LLM calls use Kimi K2.6.

nodes.label: Shared embedder BGE-m3
nodes.rationale: One shared local embedder — BGE-m3, 1024-dimensional and multilingual — is used wherever a system permits it. 'Where the system allows it' is the load-bearing qualifier: a system that locks in its own embedder breaks the shared condition.

nodes.label: Per-run spend ledger and --max-spend
nodes.rationale: Every run writes a spend ledger and respects a `--max-spend` cap, and the document states that every cost number it publishes is backed by that per-run ledger in the harness output. This is the provenance for the $1.40 / $15.67 / $3.48 figures.

nodes.label: Zero-LLM-credit graph construction
nodes.rationale: Building the graph costs $0 in LLM credits: graphify extracts with tree-sitter (deterministic, about 40 languages) plus a local embedder, and an unset API key produces zero credits. Most memory and semantic-retrieval systems instead pay a per-document LLM ingest cost.

nodes.label: Key-fact coverage grading
nodes.rationale: Answers are graded by Kimi K2.6 against a gold set of atomic key facts a correct answer must contain, and every verdict cites a verbatim quote from the answer. Grades are therefore auditable rather than a single opaque score.

nodes.label: Coverage formula
nodes.rationale: The QA-accuracy metric is `coverage = (covered + 0.5 * partial) / total` over the gold atomic key facts — partial credit at half weight. Every accuracy percentage in this document (45.3%, 76%, 82.0%, ...) is that quantity, not exact-match.

nodes.label: Blind judge validation (90.6%, kappa 0.81)
nodes.rationale: The Kimi K2.6 judge was blind-validated against a second, independent judge on a sampled set: 90.6% agreement, Cohen's kappa 0.81 (substantial agreement). The document notes most published memory benchmarks disclose no judge validation at all, so the grading itself can be audited here.

nodes.label: LOCOMO dataset (n=300)
nodes.rationale: LOCOMO (`locomo10.json`, n=300) is a multi-session conversational QA dataset and the corpus behind the headline memory numbers. Datasets are not redistributed; the harness documents the expected local layout.

nodes.label: LongMemEval-S dataset (n=50)
nodes.rationale: LongMemEval-S is the English subset at n=50, a long-horizon conversational-memory suite. The small n is itself a condition on the 76% / 74% / 70% figures reported against it.

nodes.label: ERPNext code corpus (~1M LOC)
nodes.rationale: The code-intelligence corpus is frappe/erpnext, a roughly 1M-LOC real-world production Python repository. Every code-suite and temporal number in this document is measured on that one repo.

nodes.label: Cross-referenceable academic datasets
nodes.rationale: LOCOMO and LongMemEval are the same academic datasets other memory systems already report on, so graphify's results are cross-referenceable against published third-party numbers rather than being self-defined.

nodes.label: Competing systems run as in-harness adapters
nodes.rationale: mem0 and supermemory are run self-hosted as adapters inside graphify's harness, wired through a proxy so their own LLM calls also use Kimi K2.6. Baselines (BM25, dense RAG, hybrid RRF) retrieve from the same harness-built index, which is why their ingest cost is listed as $0 (shared index).

nodes.label: LOCOMO QA accuracy 45.3%
nodes.rationale: graphify (graph-expand) scores 45.3% QA accuracy on LOCOMO n=300 — +18 points over mem0 (27.3%), +14 over BM25 (31.3%), and within 4.4 points of supermemory (49.7%) at about a tenth of supermemory's ingest cost. Condition: Kimi K2.6 reader and judge, BGE-m3 embedder, identical budgets, graphify's harness, last updated 2026-07-05.

nodes.label: LOCOMO retrieval recall@10 0.497
nodes.rationale: graphify (graph-expand) reaches recall@10 of 0.497 on LOCOMO n=300 — the best retrieval recall of any system tested — versus BM25 0.362, supermemory 0.149 and mem0 0.048 (about 10x mem0). Condition: same harness, shared BGE-m3 index for the baselines; the supermemory recall figure is embedder-confounded.

nodes.label: LongMemEval-S 76% (tied best)
nodes.rationale: On LongMemEval-S (n=50, English subset) graphify (graph-expand) scores 76% QA accuracy with recall@10 0.844, tying dense RAG for best QA while dense RAG edges it on recall (0.848). Hybrid RRF and the SurrealDB engine score 74%; BM25 and mem0 score 70%, with mem0 at recall 0.344.

nodes.label: graph-expand configuration (primary)
nodes.rationale: graph-expand is graphify's primary benchmarked configuration — seeds plus graph expansion — and is the row the headline 45.3% / 0.497 / 76% figures come from. Bold in the tables marks this primary configuration, not the column maximum.

nodes.label: graphify SurrealDB-engine configuration
nodes.rationale: A second graphify configuration scores 43.3% QA / 0.485 recall@10 on LOCOMO and 74% / 0.833 on LongMemEval-S, at $0 ingest on the shared index. It is the row the documented reproduction command actually invokes (`--adapters graphify_v1_surreal`); the 45.3% graph-expand headline is a separate adapter in the same harness.

nodes.label: Seed-only ablation 42.7%
nodes.rationale: Removing graph expansion (seeds only) still scores 42.7% on LOCOMO at the same ~$1.40 ingest, so most of the accuracy holds at the cheapest setting and graph expansion accounts for roughly the last 2.6 points.

nodes.label: supermemory comparison system
nodes.rationale: supermemory scores the highest raw LOCOMO QA accuracy at 49.7%, but at recall@10 0.149 (about 3x worse retrieval) and $15.67 ingest — roughly 11x graphify's $1.40. Its recall number is embedder-confounded by its self-host's own 768-d English-only embedder.

nodes.label: mem0 comparison system
nodes.rationale: mem0 scores 27.3% QA / 0.048 recall@10 on LOCOMO at $3.48 ingest, and 70% / 0.344 on LongMemEval-S. graphify retrieves the right memory about 10x more often and answers +18 points more accurately on LOCOMO.

nodes.label: BM25 lexical baseline
nodes.rationale: Classic lexical retrieval scores 31.3% QA / 0.362 recall@10 on LOCOMO and 70% / 0.710 on LongMemEval-S, at $0 ingest because it reads the shared harness-built index. It is the floor the graph is measured against.

nodes.label: Dense RAG baseline
nodes.rationale: Dense retrieval over the shared BGE-m3 index scores 41.3% / 0.439 on LOCOMO and 76% / 0.848 on LongMemEval-S — the one baseline that ties graphify's best QA score, and it beats graphify slightly on LongMemEval recall.

nodes.label: Hybrid RRF baseline
nodes.rationale: Reciprocal-rank-fusion of lexical and dense retrieval scores 43.3% / 0.493 on LOCOMO and 74% / 0.822 on LongMemEval-S at $0 ingest — the strongest classic baseline, within 2 points and 0.004 recall of graphify's LOCOMO headline.

nodes.label: Embedder confound on recall comparison
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-recall is not a clean axis for supermemory: its self-host locks in its own 768-d English-only embedder instead of the shared 1024-d multilingual BGE-m3, so the 0.149 figure carries a starred caveat. The document names QA accuracy — a shared Kimi reader and judge over each system's hits — as the clean comparison instead.

nodes.label: LOCOMO memory ingest cost ~$1.40
nodes.rationale: graphify's LOCOMO (n=300) memory ingest costs about $1.40 against supermemory's $15.67 and mem0's $3.48 — roughly 11x cheaper than supermemory. Condition: measured under the harness's per-run spend ledger with all LLM calls priced at Kimi K2.6 via Moonshot.

nodes.label: Fixed coding agent (crosstool suite)
nodes.rationale: The code suite holds the agent fixed — Claude Opus 4.8, at most 14 turns, a grep/read/list floor plus exactly one code-intelligence tool — and varies only which code-intelligence tool it is given. Note the code suite's model differs from the memory suite's Kimi K2.6.

nodes.label: ERPNext coverage 70.8% -> 82.0%
nodes.rationale: Giving the fixed agent one graphify tool lifts key-fact coverage on ERPNext from 70.8% (a grep-and-read baseline) to 82.0%, at about 140K tokens per query. Conditions that bound this figure: n=6 graded questions, one ~1M-LOC repo, Claude Opus 4.8 at most 14 turns.

nodes.label: Context-stuffing anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Packing the whole repo into every turn costs roughly 20x the tokens for lower key-fact coverage than the ~140K-tokens-per-query graphify path. Graph retrieval is presented as paying for itself in accuracy against both raw-file search and context stuffing.

nodes.label: Temporal sub-suite: 689 weekly AST checkpoints
nodes.rationale: The code suite includes a temporal sub-suite of 689 weekly AST checkpoints of ERPNext spanning 2011 to 2026, each built deterministically with no LLM. It exists to show how retrieval behaves as a codebase grows over 15 years.

nodes.label: 15-year graph growth (7x nodes, 17x edges)
nodes.rationale: ERPNext's graph goes from 3,069 nodes / 2,900 edges / 1,032 files at the 2011-06-08 checkpoint to 22,620 nodes / 48,710 edges / 3,758 files at 2026-06-24 — about 7x in nodes and 17x in edges. The stated reading: as the codebase grows, plain lexical retrieval finds less of the answer while graph and semantic retrieval scale with it, and AST extraction stays stable.

nodes.label: Measurement conditions and vintage (2026-07-05)
nodes.rationale: The document states it was last updated 2026-07-05; every figure in it is conditioned on that vintage plus one shared model (Kimi K2.6), one shared embedder where permitted (BGE-m3), identical token budgets, and graphify's own harness. No graphify version number is stated anywhere in the document, so version is an unrecorded condition.

nodes.label: Reproduction procedure
nodes.rationale: Reproduction requires `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` and datasets fetched into the harness's documented local layout; runs are `python memory/runner.py --phase 3 --split locomo --n 300 --adapters graphify_v1_surreal --cn natural --workers 6 --max-spend 15` and `python crosstool/run.py --repo erpnext --max-spend <budget>`. The published memory command reproduces the 43.3% SurrealDB row, not the 45.3% graph-expand headline.

nodes.label: graphify CHANGELOG slice 0.9.23-0.9.34
nodes.rationale: This is a slice of graphify's CHANGELOG.md taken at commit 07b9143d (tag v0.9.34), covering only versions 0.9.34 down to 0.9.23 — the range this knowledge-base repo's mise pin has actually resolved. The full changelog is 359 KB / ~1,700 lines; the slice is 32 KB. Full release notes per version live at https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/releases.

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.34 (unreleased)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.34 is marked (unreleased) in this changelog slice. Its six entries are all fixes: C# receiver typing per lexical declaration scope (#2472), `graphify path`/MCP `shortest_path` becoming direction-respecting by default (#2487), semantic extraction surviving dict-shaped hyperedge members (#2486), `merge-graphs` no longer dropping hyperedges (#2484), `build_from_json` reading hyperedges from both slots (#2485), and the skill flow shipping `community_name` on nodes (#2490).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.33 (2026-08-05)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.33, dated 2026-08-05: C# `partial class` merge keyed on assembly as well as namespace/name (#2411), `graphify update` keeping cross-file member-call and `indirect_call` edges into unchanged files (#2437/#2438), `graphify extract` refusing to silently substitute an empty result when a worker crashes (#2444/#2445), and `graphify install` printing a one-time pointer to the hosted platform.

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.32 (2026-08-01)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.32, dated 2026-08-01. Its headline is tier-aware merge with the `_origin` provenance marker (#2333/#2334/#2336), plus `update` preserving the `directed` flag (#2342), non-string node-id coercion (#2326), `query` rendering the true induced subgraph (#2323), `update` writing `manifest.json` to the target (#2316), narrower `coverage/` and `GRAPHIFY_OUT` pruning, C#/Kotlin/Ruby resolution fixes, and a dedup perf improvement.

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.31 (2026-07-30)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.31, dated 2026-07-30. Its only Feature entry is MCP SDK dual-compatibility with 1.x and 2.x (#2308), lifting 0.9.30's `mcp<2` cap. The rest are fixes: per-method C# receiver typing (#2299), SQL cross-file table references (#2324), `path`/`explain` no longer printing reversed hops (#2309), scalar `export const` nodes (#2266), Go predeclared-function filtering (#2313), `explain` refusing ambiguous names (#2233), and a project-scoped Antigravity install path (#2319).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.30 (2026-07-29)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.30, dated 2026-07-29. It pinned `mcp` below 2.0 to unbreak fresh installs (#2277/#2279/#2291), fixed `.tsx` absolute-path id leaks (#2262), re-anchored warm AST-cache ids after a corpus move (#2257), fixed two Bedrock backend defects (#2287, #2284), preserved edge direction in `merge-graphs` (#2261), and bounded the MCP server's multi-project graph-context cache (#2268).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.29 (2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.29, dated 2026-07-28: a general backstop canonicalizing absolute-path/machine-slug node ids out of edge endpoints (#2231/#2243), the post-commit hook refusing to overwrite an unreadable `graph.json` (#2251), removal of false JS/TS closure `indirect_call` edges (#2241), a Windows focus-stealing console fix (#2253), normalized rationale labels (#2206), indexing of `.env.example`-style templates (#2184), an Obsidian dot-label export fix (#2205), and Scala self-type `requires` edges (#2052).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.28 (2026-07-27)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.28, dated 2026-07-27, is mostly about incremental extraction: keeping cross-file edges whose target file was not in the batch (#2211/#2213), no longer pruning alive files as deleted (#2210), and no longer reusing stale community labels (#2218). It also normalized `--no-cluster` graphs' `edges` vs `links` key (#2212), scoped platform uninstall to `project_dir` (#2215), NFC-normalized manifest keys on macOS (#2221), and extracted Swift computed/observed properties (#2181).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.27 (2026-07-26)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.27, dated 2026-07-26, is the largest entry in this slice. Highlights: installers no longer clobbering an unparseable settings file (#2167), incremental `extract --no-cluster` no longer overwriting the full graph (#2169), Python decorator edges (#2154), JS/TS `baseUrl`/`paths` resolution (#2153), root-relative `stat-index.json` (#2199), legacy field-alias folding in `build_from_json` (#2194), cross-file `concept` node merging (#2182), and namespace-aware C# member-call resolution (#1609).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.26 (2026-07-25)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.26, dated 2026-07-25: `query`/`explain` no longer fabricating `indirect_call` edges to class definitions (#2137), a Windows-backslash interpreter allowlist for the post-commit hook (#2126), the hook rebuild timeout finally armed on Windows via `threading.Timer` (#2148), bash `calls` edges into `source`d files (#2141), variable-path bash `source` resolution (#2079), and UTF-8-BOM-tolerant ignore-file reading (#2163).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.25 (2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.25, dated 2026-07-22, carries only two entries and both are non-code-behaviour: the project relicensed from MIT to Apache License 2.0, and `.graphifyinclude` handling was removed outright (#2112). It is the licensing/removal boundary in this slice.

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.24 (2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.24, dated 2026-07-22: a bounded XAML code-behind scan, the sensitive-file filter no longer dropping topic docs and real source (#2106), `calls` edges resolving through aliased Python imports (#2082), dedup preserving node attributes on an exact-ID collapse (#2091), the `claude-cli` backend reading the CLI's structured-output channel (#2076), grouped `explain` cut-connection output (#2009), `query` no longer printing `calls` edges backwards (#2080), and an MCP `token_budget` for `get_neighbors`/`get_community` (#2069).

nodes.label: graphify 0.9.23 (2026-07-21)
nodes.rationale: Release 0.9.23, dated 2026-07-21, is the oldest version in this slice and the oldest this repo's pin has ever resolved. It fixed call-site line reporting, `query` silently dropping the answer past its output budget, `uninstall` destroying a user-authored `### graphify` section (#2062), non-deterministic `path` routes and wrong hop relations (#2074), `cluster-only --no-label` poisoning the label sidecar (#2073), basename-keyed ghost-duplicate merges (#2068), and scan-root-dependent Python import resolution (#2072).

nodes.label: path is direction-respecting by default (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2487, thanks @luliaz0601) `graphify path` and the MCP `shortest_path` tool respect edge direction by default instead of running on an undirected view, so a returned path no longer traverses edges backwards. Direction is recovered from the stored `_src`/`_tgt` markers; `--undirected` (CLI) or `undirected=true` (MCP) restores the old ignoring-direction search, and when no directed path exists the command says so instead of silently returning a reversed one.

nodes.label: dict-shaped hyperedge members no longer abort merge (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2486, thanks @adminwat) semantic extraction no longer aborts at merge with a `TypeError` when a hyperedge carries dict-shaped members. Members are normalized to ids, or dropped with a warning, so a single malformed hyperedge can no longer destroy a completed extraction.

nodes.label: merge-graphs no longer drops hyperedges (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2484, thanks @sortakool, approach from @oleksii-tumanov in #1691) `graphify merge-graphs` stops dropping hyperedges: hyperedge ids and member ids are relabeled with the per-repo prefix, both inputs' hyperedges are unioned instead of one clobbering the other, and the result is written to both the top-level and nested slots.

nodes.label: build_from_json reads hyperedges from both slots (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2485, thanks @sortakool) `build_from_json` reads hyperedges from both the top-level and the nested `graph` slots, so label and re-cluster runs no longer silently empty a graph's hyperedge set; a full validation wipeout is now reported loudly instead of passing quietly.

nodes.label: graph.json ships community_name on nodes (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2490, thanks @PapiScholz) the skill flow passes the curated community labels to `to_json`, so `graph.json` ships with `community_name` on nodes instead of dropping it. Before this version, a graph written by the skill flow carried cluster ids without their curated names.

nodes.label: C# receiver typing per lexical declaration scope (0.9.34)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.34 (#2472, thanks @JensD-git) C# receiver typing no longer drops a true call when a same-named variable is declared untypeably elsewhere in the method. Receiver types are tracked per lexical declaration scope and resolved by the call's position, so a typed `static` local-function parameter still resolves even when an `out var` reuses the name in the enclosing body. This explicitly fixes a regression introduced in 0.9.32 (#2346); cross-method independence (#2299) and field-conflict poisoning are unchanged, and an `out var` receiver itself remains untyped.

nodes.label: partial class merge keys on assembly (0.9.33)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.33 (#2411, thanks @JensD-git) the C# `partial class` merge introduced in 0.9.32 (#2332) stops conflating two same-named classes living in different assemblies. The merge now keys on assembly — the nearest ancestor directory containing a `.csproj`/`.fsproj`/`.vbproj` — in addition to namespace and name; a corpus with no project file keeps merging by namespace and name as before.

nodes.label: update keeps cross-file calls into unchanged files (0.9.33)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.33 (#2437/#2438, thanks @aryanbonigala) `graphify update` no longer drops member-call and `indirect_call` edges from a changed file into an unchanged target. Incremental re-resolution now sees the unchanged corpus — its nodes, `contains`/`method` edges, and the `_callable` markers, which now persist to `graph.json` like `_origin` — so cross-file calls survive an incremental rebuild while edges to a genuinely removed target are still evicted.

nodes.label: extract fails loudly on worker crash; --allow-partial (0.9.33)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.33 (#2444/#2445, thanks @Baziar) `graphify extract` stops silently substituting an empty result when a worker crashes: a `BrokenProcessPool` now triggers the sequential fallback instead of being swallowed per future, a failed worker file is retried sequentially rather than merged as empty, and a whole-pass AST failure on a fresh build exits non-zero instead of writing a zero-node graph. `--allow-partial` opts into a best-effort partial graph.

nodes.label: install prints hosted-platform pointer (0.9.33)
nodes.rationale: From 0.9.33, `graphify install` prints a one-time pointer to graphify's hosted platform after the setup summary, noting that early access is open free before the public v1 launch. It is an output-only change to the install flow.

nodes.label: tier-aware merge and the _origin marker (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2333/#2334/#2336) incremental extraction and `_rebuild_code` stopped dropping a file's other tier. Node/edge ownership had been keyed on `source_file` alone, so a semantic re-extract deleted a doc's AST headings and a full rebuild deleted document AST nodes. Merge is now tier-aware — an AST re-extract replaces only AST nodes and keeps the semantic layer, and vice versa — the `_origin` provenance marker is backfilled on load so old graphs self-heal, and the full-rebuild drop is scoped to sources actually regenerated.

nodes.label: update preserves the directed flag (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2342, thanks @Rishet11) `graphify update` preserves the graph's `directed` flag instead of rebuilding it undirected, so God-node and path ranking keep their direction on both the clustered and the `--no-cluster` rebuild paths.

nodes.label: non-string LLM node ids coerced, not fatal (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2326, thanks @Rishet11) a numeric or otherwise non-string node id coming from an LLM fragment no longer aborts the build with a `TypeError`; ids are coerced consistently across nodes, edges, and hyperedges.

nodes.label: query renders the real induced subgraph (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2323, thanks @Rishet11) `graphify query` renders every edge between visited nodes rather than only the traversal-tree edges, so the returned subgraph matches the real induced subgraph. On versions before 0.9.32 a query result understated the connectivity among the nodes it returned.

nodes.label: update writes manifest.json to the target (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2316, thanks @Rishet11) `graphify update` writes `manifest.json` into the target's own `graphify-out` instead of the current working directory, so running it from elsewhere can no longer prune the target's manifest rows.

nodes.label: coverage/ and GRAPHIFY_OUT prune scoping (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.32 narrowed two over-broad prunes: a real Python package named `coverage/` is no longer silently dropped because the prune is gated on coverage-report artefacts (#2339, thanks @Manoj21k), and a custom `GRAPHIFY_OUT` name no longer prunes every same-named directory in the tree — only the configured output path is excluded (#2273, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

nodes.label: C# out var/is/case receivers and partial-class merge (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2346, thanks @JensD-git) C# member calls resolve for receivers declared inline via `out var`, `is`, `case`, and switch-arm patterns, and members of a `partial class` split across files attach to one merged class node so cross-half calls resolve (#2332). This change is also the source of the receiver-typing regression later fixed in 0.9.34 (#2472).

nodes.label: Kotlin anonymous object members extracted (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2347) members of a Kotlin anonymous object (`object : Foo { ... }`) are extracted, together with their `implements` and `calls` edges. Before 0.9.32 those members produced no graph nodes.

nodes.label: Ruby mixin canonicalization and lexical scoping (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2302, thanks @FolatheDuckofDuckingburg) Ruby mixins declared with compact or nested syntax resolve and a qualified external mixin can no longer fabricate a phantom hub: `module Foo::Bar` and `module Foo; module Bar` canonicalize to the same fully-qualified label, `include`/`extend`/`prepend` keep the full constant path, and resolution is scoped and lexical so `extend ActiveSupport::Concern` no longer binds to a local module named `Concern`.

nodes.label: dedup drops an O(nodes x components) scan (0.9.32)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.32 (#2328, thanks @stupidprogrammer4) dedup drops an O(nodes x components) scan in remap construction, with identical results — a pure performance change, explicitly stated to be output-equivalent.

nodes.label: MCP server dual-compatible with SDK 1.x and 2.x (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.31's Feature entry (#2308, thanks @NiSHoW): the MCP server is dual-compatible with SDK 1.x AND 2.x, lifting the `mcp<2` cap 0.9.30 introduced to `mcp>=1,<3`. The 2.0 SDK removed the low-level decorator API, so `_build_server` binds the same handlers via 1.x decorators or 2.x `on_*` constructor callbacks picked at runtime, and adapts `Tool.inputSchema`, `Resource.uri` (plain `str` in 2.x), and the dropped `AnyUrl` re-export. Verified with full stdio handshakes under mcp 1.29 and 2.0.

nodes.label: mcp pinned below 2.0 to unbreak installs (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.30 (#2277/#2279/#2291) the `mcp` dependency was pinned below 2.0 so a fresh `graphifyy[mcp]`/`graphifyy[all]` install works again. `mcp` 2.0.0 dropped the `mcp.types.AnyUrl` re-export and the `Server` decorator-registration API that `graphify/serve.py` used, so an unpinned resolve broke `graphify-mcp` on every new install with an `ImportError`. The `mcp` and `all` extras required `mcp>=1,<2` (resolving to 1.29.0) and `starlette>=1.3.1,<2`; adapting to mcp 2.x was tracked as a follow-up and shipped in 0.9.31.

nodes.label: C# receiver typing is per-method, not per-file (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2299, thanks @JensD-git) C# member calls on a typed receiver stop dropping true `calls` edges when the same local name is reused across methods. Receiver typing had been per-file and poisoned a name on any conflicting or untypable rebind anywhere in the file; it became per-method, mirroring the Java resolver, so an untypable `var x = ...` in one method cannot delete a typed-parameter call edge in another.

nodes.label: SQL cross-file table references resolve (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2324) SQL cross-file table references — for example a prisma migration referencing a table created in an earlier one — resolve to the real table node instead of leaking an absolute-path id and losing the foreign key. References mint a sourceless stub that collapses onto the real definition, and identifiers are normalized so a quoted definition (`"public"."users"`) matches an unquoted reference (`public.users`).

nodes.label: path/explain recover direction from _src/_tgt (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2309) `graphify path` and `explain` stop printing reversed hops: they recover edge direction from the stored `_src`/`_tgt` markers rather than the persisted endpoint order, so a `graph.json` written with flipped storage order — older graphs, raw dumps, merge-driver output — renders the true direction.

nodes.label: export const scalar emits a node (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2266, thanks @oleksii-tumanov) `export const X = <scalar>` emits a graph node, so a named import of a scalar export is no longer left dangling.

nodes.label: Go predeclared functions no longer fabricate calls (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2313, thanks @PathGao) Go predeclared functions (`make`, `len`, `append`, `new`, ...) no longer fabricate call edges to same-named user symbols. The filter is scoped to Go bare-identifier callees so it cannot affect other languages or same-file method calls.

nodes.label: explain refuses an ambiguous name (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2233, thanks @0bLoM) `graphify explain` refuses and lists the candidates when a name matches symbols in more than one file, instead of silently resolving to an arbitrary one. Before 0.9.31 an ambiguous `explain` answered confidently about whichever symbol it happened to pick.

nodes.label: Antigravity install honors project scope (0.9.31)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.31 (#2319, thanks @MalikHaroonKhokhar) the Antigravity install workflow no longer hardcodes the global skill path for a project-scoped install. Before 0.9.31, a project-scoped Antigravity install still wrote to the global skill location.

nodes.label: .tsx parsed with the TSX grammar; no id leak (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.30 (#2262) TypeScript `.tsx` files stop leaking absolute-path / machine-slug ids into edge endpoints. The symbol-resolution pass had parsed `.tsx` with the plain TypeScript grammar, so JSX misparsed and nested handlers floated to top level, emitting `calls` edges whose source was an absolute-stem id for a caller with no node. `.tsx` now uses the TSX grammar, a `calls` edge is never emitted from an unowned source, and a general backstop canonicalizes any node-less absolute-derived endpoint.

nodes.label: warm AST cache ids re-anchored after a move (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.30 (#2257, thanks @Kaushik2003) a warm AST-cache hit after a corpus move or clone no longer replays node ids minted under the original root. Cached ids are stored root-relative and re-anchored on read, matching the manifest and stat-index portability contracts.

nodes.label: Bedrock backend: text block and timeout honored (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.30 fixed two Bedrock backend defects (both thanks @zhiyanliu): it reads the first *text* block of a Converse response instead of blindly indexing block 0, so reasoning-capable models that emit a reasoning block first no longer parse to zero nodes (#2287); and it honors `GRAPHIFY_API_TIMEOUT` and `GRAPHIFY_MAX_RETRIES` instead of botocore's silent 60s default, so long generations no longer die with a read timeout (#2284).

nodes.label: merge-graphs preserves edge direction (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.30 (#2261, thanks @hopstreax) `merge-graphs` preserves edge direction instead of rewiring import edges to the importing file. Merged graphs produced before 0.9.30 can therefore carry inverted import edges.

nodes.label: MCP graph-context cache is bounded LRU (0.9.30)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.30 (#2268, thanks @Kkartik14) the MCP server's multi-project graph-context cache became a bounded LRU — default 8, configurable via `GRAPHIFY_MAX_CONTEXTS` — instead of growing unbounded per project.

nodes.label: general backstop canonicalizes absolute-path ids (0.9.29)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.29 (#2231/#2243) absolute-path / machine-slug node ids stop leaking into edge endpoints. Module-top-level `indirect_call` sources, bash `source`/script-invocation targets, and other producers that minted an id from an absolute path are canonicalized to the root-relative node id by a general backstop, so `graph.json` link endpoints are portable across machines and clones.

nodes.label: post-commit hook refuses to overwrite an unreadable graph (0.9.29)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.29 (#2251) the post-commit hook no longer overwrites an existing `graph.json` it merely failed to read. If the existing graph is over the size cap or unparseable, the rebuild refuses to write — matching the CLI — instead of silently replacing it with a code-only extraction; the `--no-cluster` write is also atomic with a protected-graph backup.

nodes.label: JS/TS closure params shadow outer names (0.9.29)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.29 (#2241, thanks @Yyunozor) false `indirect_call` edges from JS/TS closure arguments are gone: a closure parameter such as `r` in `rows.map(r => ...)` now shadows outer names, so it no longer binds to a corpus-wide callable of the same name.

nodes.label: .env template files indexed, real .env excluded (0.9.29)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.29 (#2184, thanks @SyedFahad7) committed `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` files are indexed instead of being dropped by the sensitive-file filter, while real `.env` files and templates under a secrets directory stay excluded.

nodes.label: incremental no longer prunes alive files as deleted (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2210) incremental extraction stops pruning alive files as "deleted". The stale-source check had compared graph paths to the scan with a raw string test and no Unicode NFC normalization, pruning any non-match without checking whether the file still exists, so macOS NFD paths and legacy basename spellings lost their nodes. It now compares NFC on both sides and is fail-closed: a source missing from the scan is pruned only when its exclusion is provable, otherwise kept with a warning.

nodes.label: incremental keeps cross-file edges out of the batch (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2211/#2213) incremental extraction stops dropping cross-file edges whose target file was not in the batch. Python relative imports and markdown reference links had emitted absolute-path-derived target ids without the `target_file` stamp the incremental canonicalization needs, so a re-extracted file's imports and references dangled or vanished; both now stamp the resolved target and canonicalize to the root-relative node.

nodes.label: shared loader normalizes edges vs links (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2212) `graphify benchmark`, the graph merge-driver, and the call-flow HTML export stop crashing or silently failing on a `--no-cluster` `graph.json`. Those graphs store edges under `edges` rather than `links`, and a shared loader now normalizes both shapes.

nodes.label: uninstall with project_dir spares the global skill (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2215) `claude`/`gemini`/`codebuddy` uninstall no longer deletes the user-global skill when called with a `project_dir`; a passed `project_dir` scopes the removal. This also fixed a CLI bug where `graphify uninstall --project` deleted the global codebuddy skill.

nodes.label: manifest keys NFC-normalized on macOS (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2221, thanks @SyedFahad7) `--update` on macOS no longer re-extracts everything when the corpus path or a filename contains non-ASCII characters: manifest keys are NFC-normalized so NFD and NFC path forms match.

nodes.label: Swift computed/observed properties emit nodes (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2181, thanks @ozdemirsarman) Swift computed and observed properties — `var body: some View { ... }`, `get`/`set`, `willSet`/`didSet` — emit graph nodes, so SwiftUI views are no longer erased from the graph.

nodes.label: no stale community labels; aggregated view over the cap (0.9.28)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.28 (#2218, thanks @bobspryn) incremental rebuilds stop reusing stale community labels, and a graph that outgrows the visualization cap keeps an aggregated view instead of deleting `graph.html`.

nodes.label: installers back up and refuse to clobber configs (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2167) `claude`/`gemini`/`codex`/`codebuddy install` stop overwriting an existing settings/hooks file they cannot parse. The installers had fallen back to an empty config on any JSON parse error and rewritten the whole file, destroying the user's settings (likely trigger: a UTF-8 BOM, the same class as #2163). They now read `utf-8-sig`, refuse to modify a file that is not a JSON object while naming the path, and back up to `<name>.graphify-bak` before any modifying write.

nodes.label: incremental --no-cluster merges forward, not overwrites (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2169) incremental `extract --no-cluster` stops overwriting the full graph with just the changed files. The raw path had written only the current run's extraction over `graph.json`, dropping every node and edge owned by an unchanged file and leaving the changed file's cross-file edges dangling on absolute-path ids. It now merges the existing graph forward with the same replace/prune semantics as the clustered path, canonicalizes cross-file edge targets, and refuses a corrupt existing graph rather than overwriting it.

nodes.label: Python decorators create graph edges (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2154, thanks @Rishet11) Python decorators create graph edges, so `affected <decorator>` finds everything a decorator touches. Builtin and stdlib decorators (`@property`, `@staticmethod`, `@dataclass`, `@functools.wraps`, ...) are excluded so they do not fabricate stub nodes or false edges.

nodes.label: JS/TS imports resolve via baseUrl and paths (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2153, thanks @Rishet11) JavaScript/TypeScript non-relative imports resolve through `jsconfig.json`/`tsconfig.json` `baseUrl` and `paths`, so an import like `import x from 'src/utils'` is no longer left dangling.

nodes.label: stat-index.json root-relative and pruned (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2199) `graphify-out/cache/stat-index.json` is stored with root-relative keys, re-anchored on load (mirroring `manifest.json`), and pruned of deleted-file entries, so a moved or cloned corpus keeps its cache hits instead of re-extracting everything and the index stops growing unbounded.

nodes.label: build_from_json folds legacy field aliases (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2194) `build_from_json` folds legacy field aliases — node `name`->`label`, `path`->`source_file`, edge `type`->`relation`, `confidence_score`->`confidence` — so nodes carrying them stop entering the graph without a label or `source_file`, where they were invisible and unmergeable. The extraction warning also breaks issues down by cause.

nodes.label: absolute source_file paths re-keyed to canonical ids (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2197) absolute `source_file` paths — for example from a Windows scan — no longer break node identity: `build_from_json` re-keys absolute-derived semantic ids to the canonical root-relative id, and the semantic cache stores normalized paths.

nodes.label: cross-file concept nodes with identical labels merge (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2182) cross-file `concept` nodes whose labels normalize identically are merged, matching the behavior already applied to near-identical labels. The merge is gated to `concept` nodes with provenance, so code/rationale/document/image nodes and the cross-repo guards are preserved.

nodes.label: namespace-aware C# member-call resolution (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.27's Feat entry (#1609, adapted from #1620 by @TheFedaikin): C# member calls on a typed receiver resolve namespace-aware, so a class name used in two namespaces resolves via `using`/scope instead of bailing. It adds `base.`/`this.field` receivers, inherited-member lookup through the `inherits` chain, and shadow-poisoning so a local shadowing a field of a different type no longer produces a wrong edge.

nodes.label: bash calls into sourced files resolve (0.9.26 and 0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.26 (#2141, thanks @HerenderKumar) gave bash calls into functions defined in a `source`d file their `calls` edges — resolution had been gated on same-file definitions — handling both `source file` and `. file`, in-corpus and single-match only. 0.9.27 (#2171, thanks @Souptik96) extended it to extensionless shebang scripts and a bare `source lib.sh` with no `./` prefix, marking the bare-name binding INFERRED since it resolves via `$PATH` at runtime.

nodes.label: bash source via a variable path resolves (0.9.26 and 0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.26 (#2079, thanks @HerenderKumar) made bash `source` edges built from a variable path resolve: `source "${BENCH_DIR}/lib/x.sh"` had baked the unexpanded `${VAR}` into a dead node id; the leading expansion is stripped and the literal suffix resolved against the script's directory, emitted as INFERRED only when it resolves to a real file. 0.9.27 (#2172) went further: a `source "${VAR}/lib.sh"` whose variable is a tracked top-level assignment (or the `dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"` idiom) resolves against the variable's real directory rather than guessing the script's own.

nodes.label: SQL routines recovered by gated raw-text scan (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2180, thanks @Souptik96) SQL `CREATE FUNCTION`/`PROCEDURE` routines with PL/pgSQL-only bodies that tree-sitter cannot parse are recovered by a raw-text scan. The scan is gated on a failed parse, so a cleanly-parsing file cannot fabricate routines from commented-out DDL or `EXECUTE` strings.

nodes.label: process pool skipped when one worker is available (0.9.27)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.27 (#2173, thanks @Souptik96) the extraction process pool is skipped when only one worker is available, falling back to in-process sequential extraction. This also removed the last case where a hung Windows hook rebuild could orphan a worker.

nodes.label: classes excluded from indirect_call edges (0.9.26)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.26 (#2137, thanks @Rishet11) `graphify query`/`explain` stop fabricating `indirect_call` edges to class definitions. The callable guard had admitted classes, so passing a class as a value (`select(Model)`, `db.get(Model, id)`, `except (ErrorA, ErrorB)`, `getattr(obj, "Name", 0)`) produced a false inferred call edge. Classes are tracked separately and excluded; direct instantiation still emits its `calls` edge. The suppression is context-blind, so a genuine higher-order class callback that IS invoked (e.g. `map(Point, coords)`) also loses its edge — the stated intended tradeoff.

nodes.label: Windows hook allowlist and rebuild timeout (0.9.26)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.26 fixed two Windows post-commit-hook defects (both thanks @Rishet11): the interpreter allowlist accepts backslash paths, where a shell `case` glob had silently emptied any interpreter path containing a backslash (#2126); and the rebuild timeout is finally armed on Windows via a `threading.Timer` fallback, since it had relied on `signal.SIGALRM` and `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT` was therefore a silent no-op letting a hung rebuild run unbounded (#2148).

nodes.label: ignore files read as utf-8-sig (0.9.26)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.26 (#2163) ignore files saved with a UTF-8 BOM are honored. `.gitignore`/`.graphifyignore`/`info/exclude` had been read as `utf-8`, so a leading BOM stayed on the first line and silently dropped the first pattern (or turned a BOM'd first comment into a bogus pattern). Both ignore read sites now use `utf-8-sig`, matching git.

nodes.label: relicensed MIT -> Apache-2.0 (0.9.25)
nodes.rationale: As of 0.9.25 (2026-07-22) graphify is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, previously MIT. Apache 2.0 adds an explicit patent grant, a patent-retaliation clause, and explicit contribution terms. Contributions made before the relicensing were submitted under MIT and remain available under those terms; the original MIT text is retained in `LICENSE-MIT` and referenced from `NOTICE`.

nodes.label: .graphifyinclude removed (0.9.25)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.25 removed `.graphifyinclude` handling entirely (#2112). The file had been non-functional since dot directories became indexed by default (#873): the loader and its matchers had no consumers, so `detect` parsed the file every run and then ignored it. The dead loader and matchers are deleted, a leftover `.graphifyinclude` no longer appears in the `unclassified` list, and `detect` prints a one-time stderr note when one is present at the scan root. The supported way to re-include ignored paths is `!` negation patterns in `.graphifyignore`.

nodes.label: XAML code-behind scan bounded and pruned (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 the XAML code-behind `.cs` scan became bounded and noise-pruning so it cannot hang. `_xaml_csharp_class_nodes` had used `rglob("*.cs")` over a project root found by walking up for a `.csproj`/`.sln`, so a standalone `extract_xaml` on a `.xaml` under a large or shared parent could resolve the root to a broad ancestor and recursively scan the whole tree. It now prunes `node_modules`/`.venv`/`.git`/dot-dirs and applies a directory cap, degrading a runaway root to a fast partial scan.

nodes.label: sensitive-file filter stops dropping docs and source (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2106) the sensitive-file filter stopped silently dropping topic docs and real source. A prose file whose slug merely ended in a keyword (`privacy-tokens.md`, `token-economics.md`) and real source like `service_account.py` were dropped with no trace, while genuine secrets (`.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `secring`, `.git-credentials`, case variants) were missed. The rebalance is net stricter on real secrets while ending the false-positive loss, and `graphify extract` plus the skill flow now NAME the skipped-sensitive files instead of printing only a count.

nodes.label: calls resolve through aliased Python imports (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2082, thanks @Yyunozor) `calls` edges resolve through an aliased Python import. `from pkg import mod as alias` (and `import pkg.mod as alias`) had recorded the import edge but dropped every downstream `alias.func()` call, so the callee looked like dead code while the import graph looked complete. The local alias binding is now tracked and the call resolves to the real callee, in-corpus only. The changelog calls this the "invisible caller" family that distinguishes graphify from grep/AST name matching.

nodes.label: dedup preserves attributes on an exact-ID collapse (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2091, thanks @Synvoya) `dedup` (default on) preserves a node's attributes when two exact-ID records from the same source file collapse. The collapse had discarded one record's fields — an AST node's `source_location`, a semantic node's `summary` — so the default path silently lost data the docs promised was merged. Non-conflicting attributes are retained deterministically regardless of chunk order, records from different files or with no source path stay isolated, and a dropped record can never stamp a false `_origin` onto the survivor.

nodes.label: claude-cli backend reads structured_output (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2076, thanks @Yyunozor) the `claude-cli` backend reads the CLI's structured-output channel instead of trusting free-form prose. Newer Claude Code treats the extraction prompt as an agentic task and reports a summary in the `result` field, which parsed to zero nodes and bisected forever. The backend now pins a JSON schema when the CLI supports it — feature-detected, with the old prompt as fallback for older CLIs — and parses the `structured_output` object.

nodes.label: explain groups cut connections by file (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2009, thanks @Yyunozor) `graphify explain` on a high-degree node groups the cut connections by file instead of printing a bare `... and N more`, so callers/callees beyond the top 20 remain visible — their file, direction, and count — without a repo-wide grep.

nodes.label: query stops printing calls edges backwards (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.24 (#2080, thanks @Yyunozor) `graphify query` stops printing `calls` edges backwards. The graph on disk was correct, but the CLI loaded it undirected and BFS/DFS collected edges in traversal order, so seeding on the callee rendered `callee --calls--> caller`. The renderer recovers the stored direction from the edge's `_src`/`_tgt` (ignoring stray or dangling values), and both CLI `query` and MCP `query_graph` show the real direction.

nodes.label: MCP get_neighbors/get_community honor token_budget (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.24's Feat entry (#2069, thanks @ojmucianski): the MCP tools `get_neighbors` and `get_community` honor a `token_budget` (default 2000) instead of rendering unbounded, so one call on a god node or a large community cannot flood the client's context. Truncation is announced at the top of the output, matching `query`, with a line count and a narrowing hint.

nodes.label: --code-only documented as an extract flag (0.9.24)
nodes.rationale: 0.9.24 documentation entries (#2071, thanks @HerenderKumar): `--code-only` is surfaced in the `extract` usage text and README, and documented as an `extract` flag rather than a `/graphify` skill flag. A second README note (#1540) warns that an older `graphifyy` in system site-packages can shadow `uv run --with graphifyy`, silently running the old version.

nodes.label: caller listings report the call-site line (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 caller / "call sites" listings report the actual call-site line rather than the caller function's definition line. `explain`, `affected`, and the MCP `get_neighbors`/`query` tools had printed the caller node's `source_location` (its `def` line) for an incoming call, so a precise-looking citation sent users to the wrong line. Every caller/relation listing now reads the traversed edge's `source_file`:`source_location`, falling back to the node's own line only when the edge has none.

nodes.label: query ranks by hop distance and shows the seed first (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 `query` stopped silently dropping the answer past its output budget. Rendered nodes had been ordered by degree, so a low-degree definition node ranked last and was cut first, the queried symbol was not guaranteed to appear, and the truncation marker sat only at the end so silence read as absence. Nodes are now ranked deterministically by hop distance from the query seeds, the named seed is always rendered first and never truncated, and a prominent notice at the TOP states how many of how many nodes were shown and how to widen the budget.

nodes.label: uninstall matches the marker heading exactly (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 (#2062) `graphify uninstall` stopped deleting a user-authored `### graphify` section. The strip had used an unanchored `## graphify` pattern that matched inside a user's H3 heading, and the "already installed" guard was a substring test, so hand-written content was destroyed. The heading is now matched only when a line is exactly the marker — mirroring the install-side #1688 hardening — across all six strip sites (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md, CODEBUDDY.md, and the H1 skill registration).

nodes.label: path is deterministic and labels real relations (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 (#2074) `graphify path` and the MCP `shortest_path` tool return a deterministic route and label each hop with the edge's actual stored relation. The route had been computed over a hash-seeded undirected view so it varied run-to-run among equal-length paths, and the printed relation was read from an arbitrarily-collapsed parallel edge so it could show `calls` on a pair carrying only `references`. Traversal is now over a sorted graph and each hop shows the real relation(s), falling back to an honest `related` when none is stored.

nodes.label: cluster-only --no-label no longer poisons the sidecar (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 (#2073) `cluster-only --no-label` stopped permanently suppressing real community labels. It had written `Community N` placeholders plus a matching signature into `.graphify_labels.json`, which the reuse path then treated as fresh forever. Placeholder-only runs no longer persist the sidecar, a stored placeholder is treated as absent so already-polluted graphs self-heal, and the watch/update rebuild got the same treatment.

nodes.label: ghost-duplicate merge keys on the full source path (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 (#2068) `build_from_json`'s ghost-duplicate merge keys on the full source path rather than the bare basename. Unrelated nodes from different files sharing a common basename (`index.md`, `README.md`) and a generic label had been silently merged onto one survivor with their edges rewired, corrupting multi-corpus doc graphs. The legitimate AST/LLM same-file merge is preserved and cross-directory false merges are eliminated.

nodes.label: Python import resolution independent of scan root (0.9.23)
nodes.rationale: In 0.9.23 (#2072) Python import resolution stopped depending on the scan root. A src-layout project lost most of its `imports`/`imports_from` edges when scanned from the repo root, because absolute imports resolved only against the scan root while file-node ids are scan-root-relative, so the dangling edges were silently dropped. Absolute imports now resolve against nested package roots detected via the `__init__.py` chain, and import edges are repointed to the real file nodes, so the graph is identical whether scanned from the repo root or from `src/`.

nodes.label: Docker MCP Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit is the host into which MCP servers are installed, so that any connected MCP client gains the servers' tools. It ships a catalog of server images and a CLI plugin (`docker mcp`) that manages profiles, tools and client wiring.

nodes.label: SQLite MCP server
nodes.rationale: The SQLite MCP server is an MCP server installed into the Docker MCP Toolkit that exposes a lightweight, persistent SQL workspace to AI clients. Its database lives at /mcp/db.sqlite inside the container, backed by a Docker named volume.

nodes.label: Six SQLite MCP tools
nodes.rationale: Installing the SQLite MCP server gives connected clients six tools: read_query, write_query, create_table, list_tables, describe_table and append_insight.

nodes.label: Connected MCP clients
nodes.rationale: Any MCP client connected to the Docker MCP gateway — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and others — automatically gains the tools of every server in the active profile.

nodes.label: Not required to use graphify
nodes.rationale: The document explicitly states it is not required to use graphify; it lives in the repo as a known-good recipe for users who want a lightweight persistent SQL workspace exposed to their AI clients alongside graphify's knowledge-graph tools.

nodes.label: Reproducible runbook
nodes.rationale: The document is framed as a reproducible runbook: prerequisites, install, verification, smoke test, storage layout, client wiring, uninstall/reset and troubleshooting, each with exact commands and expected output.

nodes.label: graphify's knowledge-graph tools
nodes.rationale: graphify's own knowledge-graph tools are the MCP surface this recipe sits beside: the SQLite server is offered as a complementary SQL workspace exposed to the same AI clients, not as a replacement for the graph tools.

nodes.label: mcp/sqlite image (catalog name SQLite)
nodes.rationale: The catalog entry `SQLite` (image `mcp/sqlite`) is marked "Archived" in catalog metadata but boots and serves correctly. The document instructs using it until the newer image is fixed upstream.

nodes.label: mcp/sqlite-mcp-server image (broken)
nodes.rationale: The newer catalog entry `sqlite-mcp-server` (image `mcp/sqlite-mcp-server`) is broken: its entrypoint `/app/.venv/bin/mcp-server-sqlite` does not exist in the published layer.

nodes.label: Docker Desktop running and healthy
nodes.rationale: The first prerequisite is a healthy Docker Desktop: `docker info` returns a Server Version, and the public socket is present at /var/run/docker.sock (or its symlink to ~/.docker/run/docker.sock).

nodes.label: docker mcp CLI plugin
nodes.rationale: The Docker MCP Toolkit CLI plugin (`docker mcp`) is the second prerequisite. It is bundled with recent Docker Desktop releases, and `docker mcp --version` should print a version string.

nodes.label: Install procedure
nodes.rationale: Installation is two commands: add the working SQLite server to the default MCP profile, then pre-pull the image. Verification of the profile contents and the tool count follows immediately.

nodes.label: docker mcp profile server add
nodes.rationale: `docker mcp profile server add default --server catalog://mcp/docker-mcp-catalog/SQLite` registers the working SQLite server into the default MCP profile.

nodes.label: Image pre-pull
nodes.rationale: `docker pull mcp/sqlite:latest` pre-pulls the image so the first tool call is fast rather than paying the image download at call time.

nodes.label: Profile verification
nodes.rationale: `docker mcp profile show default | grep -E '^[[:space:]]+name:'` should list both `fetch` (built-in) and `SQLite`, confirming the server landed in the default profile.

nodes.label: docker mcp tools count check
nodes.rationale: `docker mcp tools count` should report 15 tools after the install, up from 9 before adding SQLite — a numeric confirmation that the gateway is exposing the six new tools.

nodes.label: CLI smoke test
nodes.rationale: The CLI can call MCP tools directly (`docker mcp tools call …`), so the smoke test exercises all six tools end to end — create_table, write_query, read_query, describe_table and append_insight — and read_query should return the inserted rows with timestamps.

nodes.label: Per-call gateway boot overhead
nodes.rationale: Each `docker mcp tools call` boots a fresh gateway, costing roughly 5 seconds of overhead per call — a cost paid by CLI invocation, not by a persistent client session.

nodes.label: mcp-sqlite named volume
nodes.rationale: The database file lives in a Docker named volume `mcp-sqlite`, mounted at /mcp inside containers, so the layout is `mcp-sqlite (named volume) -> /mcp/db.sqlite`.

nodes.label: Persistence across --rm containers
nodes.rationale: The named volume persists across `docker run --rm` invocations of the SQLite MCP container, so writes from one MCP tool call are visible to the next even though each call runs a disposable container.

nodes.label: Host-side volume inspection
nodes.rationale: The volume can be inspected from the host with `docker volume inspect mcp-sqlite`, a read-only alpine mount listing /mcp, or a read-only keinos/sqlite3 mount running `sqlite3 /mcp/db.sqlite '.schema'`.

nodes.label: docker mcp client connect
nodes.rationale: `docker mcp client connect <client>` wires a client to the gateway once per client; from then on the gateway exposes every server in the active profile. `docker mcp client ls` verifies the wiring.

nodes.label: Supported client list
nodes.rationale: Supported connect targets are claude-code, claude-desktop, cline, codex, continue, crush, cursor, gemini, goose, gordon, kiro, lmstudio, opencode, sema4, vscode and zed.

nodes.label: Uninstall / reset
nodes.rationale: Reversal is three steps: remove the server from the profile, drop the database volume (`docker volume rm mcp-sqlite`, which the document flags as irreversible), and remove the image.

nodes.label: initialize EOF handshake failure
nodes.rationale: `starting client: calling "initialize": EOF` means the requested server failed its MCP handshake. Common causes are a missing entrypoint binary in the image or missing required env/secrets.

nodes.label: Direct image JSON-RPC probe
nodes.rationale: To see the real error behind a handshake failure, pipe a JSON-RPC `initialize` request (protocolVersion 2024-11-05) into `docker run --rm -i -v mcp-sqlite:/mcp <image-ref> --db-path /mcp/db.sqlite` and read the image's own output.

nodes.label: Missing entrypoint binary
nodes.rationale: A published image layer missing its entrypoint binary is a named failure mode — the `sqlite-mcp-server` failure mode, where `/app/.venv/bin/mcp-server-sqlite` does not exist.

nodes.label: --enable-all-servers vs --servers
nodes.rationale: `cannot use --enable-all-servers with --servers flag` — these gateway arguments are mutually exclusive and the caller must pick one.

nodes.label: dynamic-tools meta-tool mode
nodes.rationale: When the gateway runs with `dynamic-tools` enabled it exposes only meta-tools (mcp-add, mcp-find, …) until a profile is activated mid-session, so the real server tools stay hidden.

nodes.label: No new tools after install
nodes.rationale: A documented symptom: no new tools appear in `docker mcp tools count` after a successful install — the install is fine, but the running gateway is in meta-tool mode.

nodes.label: Profile activation remedy
nodes.rationale: Two remedies for hidden tools: invoke `docker mcp tools`, which spins up an ephemeral gateway against the default profile, or call `mcp-activate-profile` from inside an MCP session.

nodes.label: Docker MCP gateway
nodes.rationale: The Docker MCP gateway is the single endpoint clients connect to; it exposes every server in the active profile, so adding a server to the profile adds its tools to every wired client without per-client configuration.

nodes.label: Default MCP profile
nodes.rationale: The `default` profile is the set of MCP servers the gateway serves. Servers are added to and removed from it by name, and its contents are inspected with `docker mcp profile show default`.

nodes.label: fetch built-in server
nodes.rationale: `fetch` is the built-in server already present in the default profile; the expected verification output lists it alongside the newly added `SQLite`.

nodes.label: Three-pass extraction pipeline
nodes.rationale: graphify processes files in three passes: code structure (free, local), video/audio transcription (local), and semantic extraction of docs/papers/images via Claude subagents (costs tokens). Only the third pass spends API tokens.

nodes.label: Pass 1 — code structure (free)
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 extracts classes, functions, imports, call graphs, and inline comments from code files with no LLM involved and no API calls. It supports 25 languages and runs entirely locally.

nodes.label: Tree-sitter AST parsing
nodes.rationale: Tree-sitter is the parser that reads code files in Pass 1, yielding classes, functions, imports, call graphs, and inline comments deterministically across 25 supported languages.

nodes.label: Deterministic SQL extraction
nodes.rationale: SQL files get special treatment inside Pass 1: tables, views, foreign keys, and JOIN relationships are extracted deterministically rather than inferred by an LLM.

nodes.label: Code files excluded from semantic extraction
nodes.rationale: Code files are not sent to the LLM semantic extractor in the normal pipeline. If a corpus contains only code files, Pass 3 is skipped entirely; semantic extraction is reserved for docs, papers, images, and transcripts.

nodes.label: Pass 2 — video and audio transcription (local)
nodes.rationale: Pass 2 transcribes video and audio files locally with no API calls, producing transcripts that later feed the semantic pass.

nodes.label: faster-whisper transcriber
nodes.rationale: faster-whisper is the local speech-to-text engine used in Pass 2, which is why video/audio ingestion costs no API tokens.

nodes.label: God-node transcription prompt seeding
nodes.rationale: The transcription prompt is seeded with the top god nodes — the most-connected concepts in the code graph built so far — so the transcript is focused on the corpus's own domain vocabulary.

nodes.label: Transcript caching
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are cached, so re-runs skip already-processed audio and video files instead of re-transcribing them.

nodes.label: Pass 3 — semantic extraction (costs tokens)
nodes.rationale: Pass 3 runs Claude in parallel over markdown, PDFs, images, and transcripts; it is the only pass that costs tokens, and it is skipped entirely for a code-only corpus.

nodes.label: Parallel Claude subagents
nodes.rationale: Each Claude subagent reads a batch of files and outputs a JSON fragment containing nodes, edges, and any group relationships. Batches are dispatched in parallel.

nodes.label: JSON fragment merge into one graph
nodes.rationale: The per-subagent JSON fragments of nodes, edges, and group relationships are merged into a single graph — the merge step is what turns a parallel fan-out into one artifact.

nodes.label: Pre-Pass-3 format converters
nodes.rationale: Before Pass 3, optional converters turn supported pointer/binary formats into Markdown sidecars under graphify-out/converted/, so the semantic extractor only ever sees text.

nodes.label: [office] extra for .docx/.xlsx
nodes.rationale: Office files (.docx, .xlsx) are converted only when the [office] extra is installed.

nodes.label: Google Workspace shortcut conversion (opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Google Workspace shortcuts (.gdoc, .gsheet, .gslides) are opt-in via --google-workspace or GRAPHIFY_GOOGLE_WORKSPACE=1 and require an authenticated gws CLI.

nodes.label: Community detection
nodes.rationale: Communities group nodes by edge density: nodes with many connections between them end up in the same community. No embedding or vector step participates in the grouping.

nodes.label: Leiden algorithm
