nodes.rationale: BoardPage, PostsPage and MembersPage rank 2, 6 and 8 in the without-tests list because top-level React page components import many things as entry points, not because they encode domain logic.

nodes.label: cn() class-merge utility as a structural god node
nodes.rationale: cn() is a one-line Tailwind class-merging utility in src/lib/utils.ts that scores 29 edges because every component conditionally combining classes imports it. Degree centrality on a React+Tailwind frontend will surface it regardless of how aggressive the ignore filter is — the connections are real, the semantic importance is low.

nodes.label: Document and wiki entities ranked alongside code
nodes.rationale: 'Post Suggestions Modal Handoff' (a planning document under docs/design-refs/) and 'Self-Host on Azure Wiki Page' (a wiki article) appear at positions 3 and 10 of the without-tests god nodes: non-code entities are extracted as nodes alongside code and sort by edge count the same way.

nodes.label: Finding 3 — cross-language INFERRED 'surprising connections'
nodes.rationale: Both runs surface INFERRED edges between Python backend types and TypeScript frontend types under 'Surprising Connections (you probably didn't know these)' — e.g. AuthError --uses--> Member, TestStartupValidation --uses--> MemberRole. A Python class does not use a TypeScript type at runtime, so users of mixed Python/TypeScript monorepos should expect a high false-positive rate in that section.

nodes.label: Name-based similarity matching across languages
nodes.rationale: The cross-language edges are name-based similarity matches between identically-named constructs in two languages, surfaced as semantic relationships. Monorepos with shared domain vocabulary across Python and TypeScript are the corpus condition that produces them.

nodes.label: INFERRED tier flagged at avg confidence 0.62
nodes.rationale: The cross-language edges are honestly flagged INFERRED with an average confidence of 0.62 on this run, but the section header still presents them as insights worth investigating — the tag is correct while the framing overstates them.

nodes.label: PostPriorityResponse/PostPriorityConfig — a real API contract recovered
nodes.rationale: The one cross-language INFERRED edge mapping to a real design contract is PostPriorityResponse --uses--> PostPriorityConfig: the backend Pydantic schema and the frontend TypeScript type mirror each other intentionally. The relationship is real, but a developer who wrote either side already knows it — INFERRED detection here recovers a fact rather than discovering one.

nodes.label: Finding 4 — uniformly low community cohesion
nodes.rationale: Most of the 141 communities in the tests-included run score between 0.05 and 0.17 cohesion; the report itself flags 0.05 as 'weakly interconnected', and Community 0 holds 112 nodes. Offered interpretations: INFERRED cross-language edges diluting cluster signal, algorithm parameters favouring over-segmentation at this density, or a corpus genuinely lacking tight intra-cluster topology.

nodes.label: Clean three-service architecture not recovered by clustering
nodes.rationale: rsl-siege-manager has a clean backend/frontend/bot split, yet community detection produces many small low-cohesion communities instead of three large cohesive ones. The neutral reading is that the mismatch itself is the signal — graph topology does not match the obvious three-tier mental model, which surfaces that the cross-language edges are doing the work.

nodes.label: 'Should Community 0 be split?' prompt generated from low cohesion
nodes.rationale: The report's Suggested Questions section turns low cohesion scores into 'should Community 0 be split into smaller, more focused modules?' prompts. On this corpus those prompts are judged less actionable as direct architectural advice.

nodes.label: Finding 5 — Alembic and pytest docstrings as isolated nodes
nodes.rationale: The tests-included run reports 752 isolated nodes against 259 without tests, and the leading examples are identical in both: Alembic migration revision docstrings (17 migration files) parsed as standalone graph nodes. The growth from 259 to 752 is dominated by test docstrings parsed the same way.

nodes.label: 'Possible documentation gaps or missing edges' label
nodes.rationale: The report labels isolated nodes 'possible documentation gaps or missing edges'. For docstring-heavy or auto-generated files that label misleads: these are change annotations or test descriptions, not architectural entities with missing connections.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore rule for **/alembic/versions/*.py
nodes.rationale: A .graphifyignore rule for **/alembic/versions/*.py reduces the isolated-node count materially on this corpus; the review suggests users with similar setups may want a default recipe.

nodes.label: Finding 6 — suggested questions skew to graph-property meta-questions
nodes.rationale: The Suggested Questions section is dominated by graph-property meta-questions rather than domain-level prompts such as 'how does authentication flow?' or 'what enforces the siege-day invariant?'.

nodes.label: Betweenness-centrality prompts
nodes.rationale: Questions of the form 'Why does _make_siege() connect Community 12 to Community 0, 1, 3...?' have a direct answer on this corpus: the fixture creates the primary domain object, every siege-touching test uses it, and the suite spans the codebase, so it is a betweenness bridge by construction.

nodes.label: Inferred-edge audit prompts
nodes.rationale: The second class of suggested question — 'are the 17 inferred relationships involving SiegeMember actually correct?' — asks the developer to validate the tool's own low-confidence connections rather than surfacing a domain insight.

nodes.label: AMBIGUOUS-tagged path-duplicate question
nodes.rationale: The one genuinely concrete question — the relationship between bootstrap-images.ps1 and scripts/bootstrap-images.ps1 — is tagged AMBIGUOUS by the report. Its answer is concrete (the same script referenced by two slightly different paths) but it is a file-naming observation, not an architectural insight.

nodes.label: The graph build is solid; the findings target the report layer
nodes.rationale: The review's own summary of scope: the underlying graph build is solid, and every finding is about how the report layer summarizes that graph into headline metrics — specifically what those metrics surface on a well-tested cross-language full-stack web app.

nodes.label: graph.html visualization
nodes.rationale: Rated as working well: graph.html is clear, navigable and easy to filter and search, and stays useful for browsing communities even when the labelled cohesion scores are low.

nodes.label: Follow-up 1 — document a test-fixture ignore recipe
nodes.rationale: Suggested upstream follow-up: since degree centrality on covered codebases consistently surfaces test factories, documenting the ignore-pattern recipe in a 'first run on a codebase with tests' section would shorten the user's iteration loop.

nodes.label: Follow-up 2 — threshold or 'potential contract' label for cross-language edges
nodes.rationale: Suggested upstream follow-up: name-based matches between Python and TypeScript types in mixed-language repos may warrant a higher confidence threshold, or a 'potential contract' label rather than the current 'surprising connection' framing.

nodes.label: Follow-up 3 — skip or group docstring-heavy files
nodes.rationale: Suggested upstream follow-up: defaulting to skip migration versions/ directories, or detecting and grouping docstring nodes that share a structural pattern, would materially reduce isolated-node noise. The review frames all three follow-ups as observations, not change requests.
